Let <MATH_0001> be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> Let <MATH_0002> be a map of constructible
sheaves of sets on <MATH_0003>. Then the set of points <MATH_0004>
where <MATH_0005>
is surjective, resp.<SPACE_0001>injective, resp.<SPACE_0002>is isomorphic to a given map
of sets, is constructible in <MATH_0006>.
<STRUCT_0003> Let <MATH_0007> be a constructible abelian sheaf on <MATH_0008>.
The support of <MATH_0009> is constructible.
<STRUCT_0004> Let <MATH_0010> be a Noetherian ring.
Let <MATH_0011> be a constructible sheaf of <MATH_0012>-modules on <MATH_0013>.
The support of <MATH_0014> is constructible.
<STRUCT_0005>

Proof of (1).
Let <MATH_0001> be a partition of <MATH_0002> by locally closed constructible
subschemes such that both <MATH_0003> and <MATH_0004> are
finite locally constant over the parts (use
Lemma <REF_0001>
for both <MATH_0005> and <MATH_0006> and choose a common
refinement). Then apply Lemma <REF_0002>
to the restriction of the map to each part.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
The proof of (2) and (3) is omitted.

<STRUCT_0001>
The following lemma will turn out to be very useful later on.
It roughly says that the category of constructible sheaves
has a kind of weak ``Noetherian'' property.

Let <MATH_0001> be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Let
<MATH_0002> be a filtered
colimit of sheaves of sets, abelian sheaves, or sheaves of modules.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> If <MATH_0003> and <MATH_0004> are constructible sheaves of
sets, then the ind-object <MATH_0005> is essentially constant with
value <MATH_0006>.
<STRUCT_0003> If <MATH_0007> and <MATH_0008> are constructible sheaves of
abelian groups, then the ind-object <MATH_0009> is essentially constant
with value <MATH_0010>.
<STRUCT_0004> Let <MATH_0011> be a Noetherian ring.
If <MATH_0012> and <MATH_0013> are constructible sheaves of
<MATH_0014>-modules, then the ind-object <MATH_0015> is essentially constant
with value <MATH_0016>.
<STRUCT_0005>
